    (package private) void
    testClosedLoopTracksTruth()
    Checks the closed loop on a trajectory with speed and heading changes, tactical grade IMU errors and noisy pseudo-ranges every second: after convergence the position error stays below three standard deviations of the fix noise, it ends up smaller than the error of the INS-only solution for the same data, and it is consistent with the estimated covariance.
    (package private) void
    testConstructor()
     
    (package private) void
    testEpochGateAcceptsExactInterval()
    Checks the epoch gate of GNSS measurements: measurements arriving exactly one epoch interval apart are accepted, while measurements arriving earlier, or repeating a timestamp, are ignored.
    (package private) void
    testEveryImuSampleCountsWithinEpoch()
    Checks that IMU samples arriving within a Kalman epoch interval are all integrated: with a 1 s epoch interval and 100 Hz samples of a body that accelerates and then decelerates, the solution must equal the per-sample integration, not a single step using only the last sample.
    (package private) void
    testGetSetConfig()

    testGetSetCoordinateTransformation()

    testGetSetEpochInterval()

    (package private) void
    testGetSetInitialConfig()
     
    (package private) void
    testGetSetListener()
     
    (package private) void
    testGnssFixIsNotAdvancedInTime()
    Checks that a GNSS fix is used as a measurement valid at its own timestamp instead of being navigated forward in time: for a body moving at 30 m/s with error-free IMU samples and error-free GNSS measurements every second, the position right after each GNSS epoch must be the true one.
    (package private) void
    testIsUpdateMeasurementsReady()
     
    (package private) void
    testPropagate()
    Checks that propagate only keeps the Kalman filter state synchronised with the INS solution: it never runs a Kalman filter epoch, never notifies the listener, returns false, and does not turn the INS solution into a GNSS estimation.
    (package private) void
    testPropagateWhenNotReadyReturnsFalse()
     
    (package private) void
    testReset()
    Checks that reset discards measurements, estimation, state, timestamps and INS solution, so that the same GNSS measurements provided again initialise the estimator exactly as the first time.
    (package private) void
    testRotationIsIntegrated()
    Checks that the angular rate of every IMU sample is integrated: after a 10 s trajectory yawing at 0.1 rad/s, initialised with GNSS measurements at the start, the estimated yaw must be 1 rad.
    (package private) void
    testTranslationIsIntegrated()
    Checks that the specific force of every IMU sample is integrated: after moving north at 10 m/s for 10 s, initialised with GNSS measurements at the start, the estimated solution must be the per-sample navigation of the initial solution, and its position and velocity must be the true ones up to the error of the GNSS initialisation.
    (package private) void
    testUpdateKinematicsWithFreeFallSpecificForceAndRotation()
    Checks that after a GNSS fix an IMU sample with both specific force and angular rate is integrated with the ECEF inertial navigation equations, and that the first sample only initialises the time reference.
    (package private) void
    testUpdateKinematicsWithFreeFallSpecificForceAndZeroAngularRate()
    Checks that after a GNSS fix an IMU sample with specific force and zero angular rate is integrated with the ECEF inertial navigation equations, and that the first sample only initialises the time reference.
    (package private) void
    testUpdateKinematicsWithZeroSpecificForceAndAngularRate()
    Checks that after a GNSS fix an IMU sample with zero specific force and zero angular rate is integrated as a free fall, and that the first sample only initialises the time reference.
    (package private) void
    testUpdateKinematicsWithZeroSpecificForceAndRotationOnly()
    Checks that after a GNSS fix an IMU sample with zero specific force and angular rate is integrated as a free fall while the attitude is rotated, and that the first sample only initialises the time reference.
    (package private) void
    testUpdateMeasurementsWhenNotReadyThrowsNotReadyException()
     
    (package private) void
    testUpdateMeasurementsWithBodyKinematicsAndWithoutInitialAttitude()
    Checks the first GNSS measurements provided to an estimator without initial attitude after an IMU sample: the sample provided before any fix does not prevent the fix from initialising the INS solution, and a Kalman filter epoch is run with the fix as measurement.
    (package private) void
    testUpdateMeasurementsWithKinematicsAndInitialAttitude()
    Checks the first GNSS measurements provided to an estimator with an initial attitude after an IMU sample: the least squares fix initialises the position and velocity of the INS solution while the configured attitude is preserved.
    (package private) void
    testUpdateMeasurementsWithoutBodyKinematicsAndWithInitialAttitude()
    Checks the first GNSS measurements provided to an estimator with an initial attitude and without kinematics: the least squares fix initialises the position and velocity of the INS solution while the configured attitude is preserved.
    (package private) void
    testUpdateMeasurementsWithoutKalmanConfig()
    Checks that without a Kalman filter configuration GNSS measurements only initialise the position and velocity of the INS solution: no Kalman filter epoch is run, and IMU samples are navigated from the least squares fix.
    (package private) void
    testUpdateMeasurementsWithoutKinematicsAndWithoutInitialAttitude()
    Checks the first GNSS measurements provided to an estimator without initial attitude and without kinematics: the least squares fix initialises the INS solution (keeping the default attitude), a Kalman filter epoch is run with the fix as measurement, and measurements repeating the timestamp are ignored.

    • GNSS_POSITION_TOLERANCE

      private static final double GNSS_POSITION_TOLERANCE
      Tolerance, in meters, for the least squares position obtained from error-free pseudo-ranges. The only error of the solution comes from the Sagnac correction, which the least squares estimator evaluates with the range to its prior position: with the prior within 10 m of the truth (the first fix is refined once) the range to a satellite moves by 7.29e-5 rad/s * 10 m / 3e8 m/s * 2.6e7 m = 6e-5 m; hence 1e-3 m.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • GNSS_VELOCITY_TOLERANCE

      private static final double GNSS_VELOCITY_TOLERANCE
      Tolerance, in meters per second, for the least squares velocity obtained from error-free pseudo-range rates. The measurement generator projects the relative velocity onto the line of sight before applying the Sagnac rotation, while the least squares estimator projects it afterwards: both lines of sight differ by 7.29e-5 rad/s * 2.2e7 m / 3e8 m/s = 5.3e-6 rad, which for a relative velocity (including the Earth rotation term) of up to 8e3 m/s amounts to 4e-2 m/s per satellite (1.2e-2 m/s were observed in the solution); hence 5e-2 m/s.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • YAW_TOLERANCE

      private static final double YAW_TOLERANCE
      Tolerance, in radians, for the yaw integrated over the yawing trajectory. The kinematics generated by ECEFKinematicsEstimator are the exact inverse of the attitude update of ECEFInertialNavigator up to rounding errors, which after 1000 samples remain several orders of magnitude below this value; 1e-6 rad (0.2 arc-seconds) is far below the 1 rad that is lost when rotation is not integrated.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • TRUTH_VELOCITY_TOLERANCE

      private static final double TRUTH_VELOCITY_TOLERANCE
      Tolerance, in meters per second, for the velocity reached against the analytic truth of a trajectory: the navigator velocity update is the exact inverse of the kinematics estimation, so the error is the one of the initial velocity, which comes from an error-free GNSS fix (see GNSS_VELOCITY_TOLERANCE).
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • TRUTH_POSITION_TOLERANCE

      private static final double TRUTH_POSITION_TOLERANCE
      Tolerance, in meters, for the position reached against the analytic truth of a trajectory. The navigator integrates position with the trapezoidal rule (eq. 5.38), whose error is well below a micrometer, so the error is the one of the initial velocity (see TRUTH_VELOCITY_TOLERANCE) accumulated over the 10 s of the trajectory: 0.5 m, which is 200 times smaller than the 100 m travelled.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • SINGLE_STEP_MIN_DIFFERENCE

      private static final double SINGLE_STEP_MIN_DIFFERENCE
      Minimum distance, in meters, between the per-sample integration and a single integration step over the whole epoch using only the last sample: the body ends 0.5 m ahead, while a single step with the final deceleration of 2 m/s^2 would move it 1 m backwards.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • CHAIN_POSITION_TOLERANCE

      private static final double CHAIN_POSITION_TOLERANCE
      Tolerance, in meters, when comparing against the chained navigator oracle. Both sides execute the same floating point operations, so differences can only come from rounding of ECEF coordinates of magnitude 6.4e6 m (ulp of 1e-9 m).
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • CHAIN_VELOCITY_TOLERANCE

      private static final double CHAIN_VELOCITY_TOLERANCE
      Tolerance, in meters per second, when comparing velocity against the chained navigator oracle: both sides execute the same operations, so only rounding errors (below 1e-9 m/s) remain.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • CHAIN_ROTATION_TOLERANCE

      private static final double CHAIN_ROTATION_TOLERANCE
      Tolerance for each element of the body to ECEF rotation matrix when comparing against the chained navigator oracle: elements are bounded by one and both sides execute the same operations, so differences are bounded by accumulated rounding (1e-13 after 1000 samples).
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • FREE_FALL_POSITION_TOLERANCE

      private static final double FREE_FALL_POSITION_TOLERANCE
      Tolerance, in meters, for the displacement of a free fall of up to 1 s starting with a speed of up to 3.5 m/s (2 m/s per axis) against v0 * t + g * t^2 / 2. The neglected Coriolis acceleration is at most 2 * 7.29e-5 rad/s * (3.5 + 9.8) m/s = 1.9e-3 m/s^2, i.e. 1e-3 m after 1 s, and the gravity gradient over the 8.4 m travelled adds 3e-6 s^-2 * 8.4 m = 2.5e-5 m/s^2; hence 1e-2 m.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • FREE_FALL_VELOCITY_TOLERANCE

      private static final double FREE_FALL_VELOCITY_TOLERANCE
      Tolerance, in meters per second, for the velocity of a free fall of up to 1 s starting with a speed of up to 3.5 m/s against v0 + g * t: the neglected Coriolis acceleration (1.9e-3 m/s^2 at most, see FREE_FALL_POSITION_TOLERANCE) integrates to 1.9e-3 m/s; hence 5e-3 m/s.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

      Maximum position error, in meters, right after a GNSS epoch with error-free measurements and an error-free IMU. Using the fix as if it were valid one epoch earlier (or navigating it forward over one epoch) displaces a body moving at 30 m/s by 30 m; 0.5 m is 60 times smaller, while the error actually expected is the one of the least squares fix (see GNSS_POSITION_TOLERANCE).

    • testUpdateMeasurementsWithoutKinematicsAndWithoutInitialAttitude

      @Test void testUpdateMeasurementsWithoutKinematicsAndWithoutInitialAttitude() throws com.irurueta.navigation.LockedException, com.irurueta.navigation.NotReadyException, INSGNSSException
      Checks the first GNSS measurements provided to an estimator without initial attitude and without kinematics: the least squares fix initialises the INS solution (keeping the default attitude), a Kalman filter epoch is run with the fix as measurement, and measurements repeating the timestamp are ignored.
      Throws:
      com.irurueta.navigation.LockedException - if estimator is locked.
      com.irurueta.navigation.NotReadyException - if estimator is not ready.
      INSGNSSException - if estimation fails.

      Checks the first GNSS measurements provided to an estimator without initial attitude after an IMU sample: the sample provided before any fix does not prevent the fix from initialising the INS solution, and a Kalman filter epoch is run with the fix as measurement.
      Throws:
      com.irurueta.navigation.LockedException - if estimator is locked.
      com.irurueta.navigation.NotReadyException - if estimator is not ready.
      INSGNSSException - if estimation fails.

    • createSatellites

      private static List<com.irurueta.navigation.gnss.ECEFPositionAndVelocity> createSatellites(com.irurueta.statistics.UniformRandomizer randomizer, com.irurueta.navigation.frames.ECEFFrame userFrame)
      Creates a constellation of satellites in view of a user, as the existing GNSS tests do but with a seeded randomizer: one satellite per azimuth sector, at a seeded pseudo-random azimuth within the sector and elevation above the masking angle, at a typical GPS range and with a seeded pseudo-random velocity. Spreading azimuths and elevations keeps the geometry well conditioned.
      Parameters:
      randomizer - seeded randomizer.
      userFrame - frame containing the user position.
      Returns:
      positions and velocities of the satellites at time zero.

    • createGnssConfig

      private static com.irurueta.navigation.gnss.GNSSConfig createGnssConfig(double codeTrackingSD, double rangeRateTrackingSD)
      Creates the configuration used to generate GNSS measurements. Only white tracking errors are configured: there are no slowly varying range biases (signal in space, ionosphere and troposphere errors are zero), so that the errors of consecutive fixes are uncorrelated, as the Kalman filter assumes.
      Parameters:
      codeTrackingSD - code tracking error standard deviation expressed in meters. Zero generates error-free pseudo-ranges.
      rangeRateTrackingSD - range rate tracking error standard deviation expressed in meters per second. Zero generates error-free pseudo-range rates.
      Returns:
      GNSS configuration.

    • assertUpdateBodyKinematicsIntegratesSample

      private INSGNSSLooselyCoupledKalmanFilteredEstimatorTest.IntegratedSample assertUpdateBodyKinematicsIntegratesSample(INSGNSSLooselyCoupledKalmanFilteredEstimatorTest.Fixture fixture, BodyKinematics kinematics) throws com.irurueta.navigation.LockedException, com.irurueta.navigation.NotReadyException, INSGNSSException, InertialNavigatorException
      Checks the behaviour of body kinematics updates after a first GNSS fix: the first sample only sets the time reference (no navigation), a repeated timestamp is ignored, and the second sample is integrated with the ECEF inertial navigation equations over the elapsed interval, without running any Kalman filter epoch nor modifying the GNSS estimation.
      Parameters:
      fixture - inputs of the test. The fix is provided at its timestamp, the first sample at the same timestamp and the second one at twice that timestamp.
      kinematics - kinematics provided on both samples.
      Returns:
      frames estimated right after the fix and after the second sample.
      Throws:
      com.irurueta.navigation.LockedException - if estimator is locked.
      com.irurueta.navigation.NotReadyException - if estimator is not ready.
      INSGNSSException - if estimation fails.
      InertialNavigatorException - if the oracle navigation fails.
